scenarios.title: Five Humanoids — Warehouse Truck Loading
scenarios.status: Closed — accepted for controlled two-shift operation
scenarios.summary: Deliver five humanoids from signed order through site acceptance, controlled pilot, truck-loading cutover, hypercare, and operations handoff. Each robot works in a separate lane, receives an approved carton at a conveyor, and places it on a floor pallet. A robot-operated forklift loads each completed seven-carton pallet into an outbound truck.
scenarios.decision: Northstar accepted the cell for controlled two-shift use after all mandatory safety tests passed and the 14-day hypercare window exceeded the contracted throughput, mission-success, intervention, damage, and availability thresholds. A second cell remains conditional on Finance validating at least $445,200 of annual gross capacity value using actual labor and volume data.

metrics.label: Throughput
metrics.note: Target: at least 225 for two consecutive hours

scenarios.financial_note: Base-case simple payback is 3.66 years and five-year Return on Investment (ROI) is 22.2%. If Finance can monetize only 60% of available labor capacity, payback becomes 8.95 years and expansion is not approved.

risks.risk: Carton mix exceeds the validated 2–15 kilogram envelope
risks.response: Reject workflow, daily mix report, and change-control trigger

risks.risk: Forklift or pedestrian enters the robot operating zone
risks.response: Physical separation, access controls, and witnessed intrusion tests

risks.risk: Network coverage degrades inside trailer or dock
risks.response: Radio-frequency survey, redundant coverage, and local safe-state test

risks.risk: Grasp failures reduce throughput
risks.response: Representative carton tests, tuning, and exception routing

risks.risk: Critical spare lead time threatens restoration target
risks.response: Onsite minimum stock and replenishment trigger

scenarios.title: Three Quadrupeds — Night Security
scenarios.summary: Deploy three quadruped robots for human-supervised night patrol across stairs, curbs, gravel, and narrow walkways. Two robots run scheduled perimeter routes while the third rotates through charging and reserve coverage. Robots observe and report; authorized human security personnel retain all response decisions.
scenarios.decision: The pilot met all safety, privacy, patrol, alert, geofence, availability, and docking criteria. Sentinel Ridge authorized two recurring quadruped patrol posts and retained the existing fixed-post responder. Expansion beyond the approved routes requires a new route, privacy, network, and benefit review.
scenarios.financial_note: Base-case simple payback is 3.22 years when two contracted walking-rover posts are removed and one onsite responder remains. Removing only one post produces an 11.73-year payback, so that configuration does not pass the expansion screen.

risks.risk: Wireless dead zone interrupts live supervision
risks.response: Day/night survey, redundant path, and tested local safe state

risks.risk: Video records outside the approved purpose or area
risks.response: Privacy masks, retention limits, access audit, and quarterly review

risks.risk: Weather or surface exceeds the operating envelope
risks.response: Weather gate, route inspection, and recall rule

risks.risk: False alerts overload the security operator
risks.response: Shadow mode and threshold tuning reduced workload to 4.2 per night

risks.risk: Dock failure removes reserve patrol coverage
risks.response: Reserve robot, spare charger, and manual patrol fallback

demo.caption: Two quadrupeds patrol independent routes while a third remains available for charging rotation. The run demonstrates rough terrain, steps, anomaly escalation, human verification, network safe stop, sensor degradation, and low-battery docking.

closure.schedule: Completed in week 20 after a 30-night pilot
acceptance: All scheduled patrol and availability thresholds passed
Fifty witnessed critical alerts arrived within 15 seconds
Privacy masking, access, retention, deletion, and audit tests passed
Network-loss, sensor-degradation, low-battery, docking, and retrieval tests passed

lessons: Survey the route at the actual patrol hour and weather conditions
Measure false-alert workload before unattended patrol

scenarios.title: AD-01 — New Robot Through First Sale
scenarios.summary: Develop a compact mobile manipulator that moves one approved tote type weighing up to 15 kilograms along an 18-meter indoor route between two fixed stations. The program runs from observed customer workflows through Engineering Verification Test, Design Verification Test, Production Validation Test, first-customer deployment, 30-day acceptance, and a commercial release decision.
scenarios.decision: Leadership approved limited availability for the narrow two-station workflow. The first customer accepted the system, Cost of Goods Sold and pilot-build yield met the release gate, and the corrected design exceeded the mission target. General Availability remains gated by actuator second-source qualification and a qualified pipeline that can support the 82-unit development break-even screen.

metrics.label: Supplier exposure
metrics.note: Actuator second source due before General Availability

scenarios.financial_note: Customer simple payback is 1.96 years. At the $285,000 unit price and $150,000 Cost of Goods Sold ceiling, contribution is $135,000 per unit and approximately 82 units are required to recover the $10.975M development investment before other corporate costs.

risks.risk: Use-case expansion outruns requirements and safety evidence
risks.response: Release 1 limited to one tote, two stations, flat floors, and supervised recovery

risks.risk: Critical actuator supplier threatens scale schedule
risks.response: Buffer stock and second-source qualification before General Availability

risks.risk: Thermal derating prevents reliability target
risks.response: Cooling and current-limit correction passed 2,000-cycle Design Verification Test

risks.risk: Field faults cannot be diagnosed remotely
risks.response: Fault codes, telemetry bundle, replaceable-unit drill, and support gate

risks.risk: Unit cost exceeds the commercial model
risks.response: Value engineering and supplier negotiation produced $149,200 released cost

acceptance: Corrected design passed 2,000 representative Design Verification Test cycles at 98.4% mission success
Production Validation Test achieved 9 of 10 first-pass units
Released Cost of Goods Sold was $149,200 and assembly/test time was 39.4 hours

lessons: Narrow scope made safety and value claims testable
Serviceability and telemetry must be product requirements
A second source needs a dated gate, not a generic mitigation

scenarios.title: Robotics Support & Field Operations
scenarios.status: Closed — service owner accepted operating model
scenarios.summary: Stand up one traceable support chain for 250 humanoid and quadruped robots across 60 sites. The operating model connects Salesforce customer cases, ServiceNow or Zendesk workflows, field work, Jira engineering defects, robot telemetry, parts, knowledge, release readiness, and customer communications.
scenarios.decision: The executive sponsor and service owner accepted the 180-day operating model. All 250 robots and 60 sites have owned installed-product records; severity, on-call, field, parts, remote-access, continuity, and product-readiness controls are live. High-confidence predictive case automation remains a phase-two improvement and is not required for closeout.

metrics.note: Target: at least 95% of escalations complete

scenarios.financial_note: The year-one authorization includes the six-month implementation, initial 15-person operation, platform integration, telemetry, remote access, field tools, starter spares, enablement, contingency, and sponsor reserve. Vendor prices remain quote-required planning inputs.

risks.risk: Critical parts are unavailable during a site outage
risks.response: Failure forecast, depot minimums, serialized stock, and tested transfer workflow

risks.risk: Coverage demand exceeds the 15-person team
risks.response: Six-week utilization, response-miss, and skill-coverage staffing triggers
